subject: RetailX onramp: hosted commit upgrade + rateband realignment
messages:
From: Elena Rossi <elena@retailx.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: Joe Miller <joe@retailx.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Exploring a faster onramp — committing to higher monthly volume

Hi Karthik,

Quick note from our side — we've been ramping trial traffic and expect a 2.5x increase in peak API tokens over the next quarter. We'd like to explore moving from our current hosted plan (tier: Standard, 1.2M tokens/mo) to a committed band that reduces per-token spend and eases soft-throttle risk.

High-level asks:
- Target committed throughput: ~3M tokens/mo with a burst cushion for Black Friday testing.
- Prefer a monthly billing cadence and predictable rate limits per route.
- Need confirmation on latency SLOs for the cart-checkout flow (p95 target < 220ms).

Can you share a bench-mark pricing path and an ops plan for onboarding within 4–6 weeks? Happy to loop procurement once we have numbers.

Thanks,
Elena
Elena Rossi
Head of ML Platforms | RetailX
elena@retailx.com
+1 415-555-0134

Subject: Re: Exploring a faster onramp — committing to higher monthly volume

Elena — thanks for the context and the clear asks. Short answer: yes, we can design a committed band that matches ~3M tokens/month with a configurable burst pocket and preserve p95 latency targets for your critical route.

Next steps I propose:
1) I'll drop a proposed Mutual Action Plan (MAP) and pricing band (incl. burst guardrails and soft-throttle thresholds) by EOD tomorrow.
2) Vanessa (CC) will confirm ops steps for capacity reservation and a target onboarding timeline (4–6 weeks is reasonable).
3) If procurement needs a formal SOW + PO flow we'll surface our standard SOW and provide a DocuSign-ready file.

I'll attach a draft pricing sheet and MAP in my follow-up. Any constraints on contract language or an internal deadline you have for Black Friday readiness?

—Karthik

Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 09:35:00 -0700

Looping in operations details and a rough ops checklist.

Karthik / Priyom — for a 3M committed band + burst pocket we should: 
- Reserve a dedicated slot in the pool for RetailX on the 2nd GPU cluster for predictability.
- Apply a progressive soft-throttle: 100% committed -> 130% burst -> 200% emergency (pay-as-you-go overage) with automated fallback to a compatible smaller model if sustained beyond 48h.
- Enable prefix / KV caching for cart-checkout route to keep p95 under 220ms — we'll need sample traces (5–10k requests) to tune batching.
- Onboarding tasks: staging keys, model pin (v2.3), traffic mirroring for 48h, then gradual cutover.

I'll estimate the ops lead time and include a stub MAP row for each task in the spreadsheet Karthik is preparing. Priyom — can you draft the MAP deliverables and owner columns?

Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Customer Operations | Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com

Elena

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com, procurement@retailx.com
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2026 10:05:00 -0700

Joe / Procurement team — attaching the items you requested:
- RetailX_MutualActionPlan_v1.xlsx (MAP with owners, timeline, test gates)
- redwood-pricing-sheet-2026Q2.xlsx (breakdown: committed band 3.0M tokens/mo, burst up to 130% included, emergency overage billed at on-demand rates)
- SOW-RetailX-hosted-commit-draft.pdf (standard SOW with data residency and SOC2 references)

Key clarifications in the pricing sheet:
- Committed band: 3,000,000 tokens/month; monthly invoice; unit price $0.0035/token (net before discount).
- Included burst: up to 130% of committed tokens in any billing cycle in the monthly fee. Sustained usage beyond 130% will transition into emergency overage which is billed at $0.0062/token.
- Soft-throttle policy: we enforce a graded throttle starting at 150% sustained 12h. Ops will send a proactive alert at 110% sustained 6h.
- Latency SLO: p95 <220ms for the pinned model on our US cluster; will require request traces and a 48h mirror soak to guarantee.

On the fallback model: our research team has a 4-bit quantized variant of v2.3 that maintains >98% of checkout intent accuracy in our evals. We'll include it as an option in the SOW with a quality acceptance gate.

If these terms look good, sign the attached SOW and we'll issue a DocuSign envelope with the final PO-ready document. Vanessa — ops lead time looks like 3 weeks once we have signed SOW + PO.

Best,
Karthik

Karthik / Vanessa — thanks for the quick turnaround and the attachments. Reviewed with legal and we have two small asks before signing:
1) Add a PO reference field on the invoice and Net-30 payment terms (we confirm PO number will be provided within 2 business days of SOW signature).
2) Clarify the definition of "sustained" in the soft-throttle clause (we propose sustained = sustained average over a 12-hour sliding window).

If you can issue a revised SOW with those two clarifications, we can route for signature and target a June 30 effective date. We'll include the initial PO and payment contact once the SOW is updated.
